newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Price shifts draw Hungary futures focus to yen, Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Price shifts draw Hungary futures focus to yen, Sfr.

text.p: Yen and Swiss franc futures for December were in focus on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday, while only the March mark and dollar were traded on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE), traders said.
The BCE's financial section posted turnover of 6.77 billion forints, while currency futures turnover totalled 289.4 million on the BSE.
"The Japanese yen and the Swiss francs had perhaps the most interest," said BCE trader Janos Szolyka of Swap.
"As for the Swiss franc, the main reason was that it has strengthened some 1.2 forints in two days," he said, adding that the strengthening came despite the lack of any major news.
He added the Japanese currency's decline has lasted for three days.
Swiss francs closed firmer for September, December and March 1998, while the Japanese yen fell for the same instruments.
In both currencies the December maturity was the most active, with 3,310 contracts for yen and 10,300 contracts for the Swiss francs, a BCE spokesman said.
Dollar futures closed lower for March, June and September, while the German mark edged up for the same maturities plus December.

On the BSE, where only U.S. dollar, German mark and ECU currencies are traded, dollar futures fell for four maturities, while they were mostly steady for German mark, but only the March maturity saw one deal in each of mark and dollar.
March dollar fell to 176.98 forints, down 0.73, while March market advanced 21 fillers to 104.47 forints.
On the spot market the forint closed at 176.88/93 to the dollar.
